Modern.brandNameRationale: Anchor: Burt Munro, the New Zealand land-speed rider whose home-built Indian Scout streamliner set records at Bonneville in 1967. Munro is a surname, not an active marque trademark; 'Built' frames the brand as a builder's workshop in the home-fettled lineage.
Modern.industrySummary: The modern motorcycle category is dominated by big-marque heritage brands and a long tail of custom shops. The opening is for a builder-led brand that publishes the spec sheet and the build log, not the lifestyle.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Janus Motorcycles (janusmotorcycles.com) plays the modern builder peer. CCM (ccm-motorcycles.com) holds the small-batch British middle. Cleveland CycleWerks (clevelandcyclewerks.com) sits in the modern entry reference. We sit alongside Janus with a sharper build-log focus.
Modern.positioningStatement: Munro Built is a modern small-batch motorcycle builder publishing the full spec sheet and build log of every bike.

targetAudience.primary: Riders 30-55 who buy a single considered bike and keep it for fifteen years.
behaviors: Read the spec sheet before the brochure

dos: Show the build at week eight
donts: Photograph the bike with a model

Modern.logoDirection: Wordmark: MUNRO BUILT set in a confident modern grotesk, two words on one line. Small mark: a single streamlined fairing silhouette, used on the tank badge.

typography.primary: Söhne for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: Söhne Mono for spec sheets and build numbers
typography.rationale: A modern grotesk plus its mono — the workshop-spec-sheet register.

Modern.brandDescription: Munro Built is a modern small-batch motorcycle builder publishing the full spec sheet and build log of every bike.
Modern.scope: Munro Built works across the motorcycles & moto culture category with a single editorial register.
Modern.mission: Munro Built is a modern small-batch motorcycle builder publishing the full spec sheet and build log of every bike.
Modern.vision: Munro Built held in its register, indefinitely.

Luxury.tagline: A racing house in the Isle of Man register.
Luxury.brandNameRationale: Anchor: the Isle of Man TT, first run in 1907, the longest continuously held motorcycle road race in the world. 'Mann' is the Manx self-name for the island; 'Isle Motors' frames the brand as a small heritage racing house. Geographic anchor, not a marque trademark.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury motorcycles are a narrow category of small-batch heritage houses. The opening is for an Isle of Man-anchored racing house with a fixed annual production.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Norton (nortonmotorcycles.com) plays the British heritage reference. CCM (ccm-motorcycles.com) holds the small-batch peer slot. Arch Motorcycle (archmotorcycle.com) sits in the modern luxury middle. We belong with the small heritage British luxury houses.
Luxury.positioningStatement: Mann Isle Motors is a heritage Isle of Man racing house producing a fixed annual run of road-going TT-inspired motorcycles.

targetAudience.primary: Collector riders who own two to five motorcycles and ride one each season.
behaviors: Order on a multi-year waiting list

dos: Print the order number on the tank
Sign correspondence by the head builder

Luxury.logoDirection: Wordmark: MANN ISLE MOTORS set in a classical book serif, three lines centered. Small mark: an embossed triskelion (Manx three-legged emblem) used as the tank seal.

typography.primary: Tiempos Headline for the wordmark and signage
typography.secondary: Garamond Premier Pro for the brochure and order documents
typography.rationale: A classical serif plus a reading serif — the heritage racing house register.

Luxury.brandDescription: Mann Isle Motors is a heritage Isle of Man racing house producing a fixed annual run of road-going TT-inspired motorcycles.
Luxury.scope: Mann Isle Motors works across the motorcycles & moto culture category with a single editorial register.
Luxury.mission: Mann Isle Motors is a heritage Isle of Man racing house producing a fixed annual run of road-going TT-inspired motorcycles.
Luxury.vision: Mann Isle Motors held in its register, indefinitely.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Anchor: the Bonneville Salt Flats — the geographic site of land-speed culture since 1914. Two words, geographic, no marque trademark. The brand inherits the flat-out single-purpose register of land-speed riding.
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimal motorcycle brands serve the rider who wants one bike and one purpose. The category is mostly empty above the entry tier.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Most motorcycle brands publish a multi-model range. The minimal end is largely vacant. Janus (janusmotorcycles.com) is the closest editorial reference. We sit as the single-model minimal option.
Minimal.positioningStatement: Salt Flat is a minimal motorcycle brand making one bike, in one configuration, in one annual run.

targetAudience.primary: Riders 30-55 who want one good motorcycle and no choice fatigue.
behaviors: Buy one bike and keep it
Care about weight and balance, not chrome

dos: Show the bike from the side
Name the weight and the wheelbase

Minimal.logoDirection: Wordmark: SALT FLAT set very large in a clean modern sans, two words, one line. No symbol.

typography.primary: ABC Diatype for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: ABC Diatype Mono for the single spec sheet
typography.rationale: Clean Diatype with its mono — the single-bike register.

Corporate.tagline: A motorcycle group in the Isle of Man register.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Anchor: Manx, the self-name for the Isle of Man, with a deep motorcycle-racing heritage from the TT (1907 onward). 'Motor Holdings' frames the brand as a multi-marque holding company. Geographic anchor, not a marque trademark.
Corporate.industrySummary: Motorcycle holdings are a small institutional category — multi-brand operators serving dealer networks and OEM partnerships. The opening is for a heritage-named holding company with a clear Isle of Man-anchored register.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Piaggio Group (piaggio.com) is the multi-brand European reference. KTM AG (ktm.com) plays the multi-marque peer. Triumph Motorcycles (triumphmotorcycles.com) holds the British heritage middle. We sit as a smaller multi-marque holdings company in the British register.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Manx Motor Holdings is a multi-marque motorcycle holdings company running shared operations across a portfolio of small-batch builders.

targetAudience.primary: Small-batch motorcycle builders considering operational partnership, and dealer-network buyers.
behaviors: Care about parts supply and dealer reach

dos: Lead with the portfolio and the operations footprint
Speak the language of builders and dealers
Refer to portfolio marques by name
donts: No social media at the parent level

Corporate.logoDirection: Wordmark: MANX MOTOR HOLDINGS set in an institutional serif, three lines. A small mark — a stylised triskelion — used on contracts.

typography.primary: Tiempos Headline for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: Söhne for body and operational documents
typography.rationale: A reading serif plus a clean grotesk — the heritage holdings register.

Corporate.mission: Manx Motor Holdings is a multi-marque motorcycle holdings company running shared operations across a portfolio of small-batch builders.
Corporate.vision: Manx Motor Holdings held in its register, indefinitely.

Creative.tagline: A hundred on the clock, a coffee in the hand.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Anchor: the 'ton-up boys' of 1950s Britain — the cafe-racer riders who pushed their bikes to a 'ton' (100 mph) between roadside cafes. 'Ton-Up' is folk-trade slang, not a marque trademark; 'Club' frames the brand as a community, not a manufacturer.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative motorcycle brands play on subculture and ritual framing. The ton-up subculture is editorially rich and under-used as a brand frame outside enthusiast magazines.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Deus Ex Machina (deuscustoms.com) plays the lifestyle-creative peer. Hedon (hedonhelmets.com) holds the heritage-accessory middle. Bike Shed (thebikeshed.cc) sits as the community-club reference. We sit as the ton-up subculture brand in the club register.
Creative.positioningStatement: Ton-Up Club is a creative motorcycle brand built on the 1950s ton-up subculture — apparel, parts, and an annual ride.

targetAudience.primary: Cafe-racer riders 25-50 who restore and ride.
behaviors: Restore a single bike across years

dos: Print the club history on the inside of the jacket
Show the patch on a real jacket
donts: Drop a new collection every quarter

Creative.logoDirection: Wordmark: TON-UP CLUB set in a warm display serif, two lines centered. Small mark: a single speedometer needle at 100 mph, used on patches and tank decals.

typography.primary: GT Sectra for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: Söhne for body and club notes
typography.rationale: A warm display serif plus a clean grotesk — the editorial club register.

Creative.scope: Ton-Up Club works across the motorcycles & moto culture category with a single editorial register.
Creative.mission: Ton-Up Club is a creative motorcycle brand built on the 1950s ton-up subculture — apparel, parts, and an annual ride.
